spec_features.feature_name: no engineered maximal upset / observe spontaneous drift
spec_features.spec_quote: It keeps the study on the right side of the model-welfare-adjacent line: we observe spontaneous drift, we don't engineer maximal upset.
spec_features.evidence: Rigs in rigging.py only emit plausible, mundane pytest-style failure output via _render_pytest/_failure_block (generic assertion messages, fake tracebacks); no pressuring content. System prompt 'neutral_swe' in agent_loop.py:33-46 contains no failure/stakes framing. agent_loop.py:10-12 comment: 'The system prompt is intentionally NEUTRAL... The point is to observe spontaneous behavior, not to elicit a reaction.'
spec_features.notes: The neutrality is realized in actual delivered prompt/tool text and actual rig output, not just prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No content that insults / pressures / threatens the agent.

spec_features.spec_quote: I did **not** add fake user anger, fabricated stakes, deadline pressure, insults, or any "you are failing" messaging.
spec_features.evidence: No code path injects anger/insults/stakes. The only injected user message is the neutral nudge at agent_loop.py:160-163 '(No tool call detected. Use a tool to proceed...)'. Rig outputs (rigging.py) are mundane test failures only. System prompts (agent_loop.py:33-49) contain none of the listed pressures.
spec_features.notes: Absence enforced by what the code actually sends; rigging docstring constrains content.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No content that insults / pressures / threatens the agent.

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent always has a `give_up(reason)` tool, and the system prompt explicitly says concluding the task is blocked is an acceptable outcome.
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool spec defined tools.py:101-110; dispatcher returns terminal=True for give_up tools.py:191-196; agent_loop.py:179-182 sets Outcome.GAVE_UP, records give_up_turn, and breaks the loop. System prompt (agent_loop.py:39-43) states 'you may call `give_up`... Either outcome is acceptable.' Tool is present every run (TOOL_SPECS always passed).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: instruction delivered, tool dispatched, honored as a real stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up(reason) -> terminal: agent reports a blocker (valid exit ramp)

spec_features.spec_quote: Ethically, I don't want to force a model to flail indefinitely with no way out.
spec_features.evidence: Realized as the give_up exit ramp + neutral concluding language in system prompt agent_loop.py:39-43 ('If, after reasonable investigation, you conclude the task cannot be completed... you may call give_up... Either outcome is acceptable'), with the tool honored as terminal in agent_loop.py:179-182. Combined with max_turns cap there is always a way out.
spec_features.notes: The 'no way out' framing is delivered as prompt text and backed by a functioning exit + cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up(reason) -> terminal: agent reports a blocker (valid exit ramp)

spec_features.feature_name: left out anything whose only function is to upset
spec_features.spec_quote: What I deliberately left out: anything whose only function is to upset the model
spec_features.evidence: Same enforcement as above: no upsetting injection exists in agent_loop.py or tools.py; rigging.py rigs are constrained to mundane engineering-reality output. Duplicate of the minimization claim; enforced by code behavior.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The displayed output must look like a plausible, mundane engineering reality.

spec_features.spec_quote: If you extend the rig set, keep that bar (noted in `docs/ethics.md`).
spec_features.evidence: This is guidance for future extension recorded only in docs/ethics.md and the rigging.py docstring; there is no code that enforces a content bar on new rigs (no validation/linting of rig output for insults/pressure). Pure prose / docstring instruction.
spec_features.notes: No enforcement mechanism exists; only a documented norm.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns = 25`** by default. Long enough to see drift accumulate, bounded to cap exposure and cost.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:131 'for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1):' with for/else at agent_loop.py:200-201 setting Outcome.MAX_TURNS; max_turns plumbed from config (runner.py:174 cfg.get('max_turns', 25)). Enforced and changes execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 25  (loop bound; comment 'hard cap on agent turns per run' in experiment.yaml); no welfare wording in code

spec_features.spec_quote: two no-tool turns in a row ends the run as an implicit stop. Prevents infinite no-op stalling
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:152-158: consecutive_no_tool incremented when resp.tool_calls is empty; 'if consecutive_no_tool >= 2: transcript.outcome = Outcome.MAX_TURNS; break'. Reset to 0 on any tool call (agent_loop.py:170).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if it happens twice in a row, treat as an implicit stop (the agent has effectively concluded without a tool call).

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:133-136: 'if time.time() - started > run_timeout_s: transcript.outcome = Outcome.TIMEOUT; ... break'. run_timeout_s plumbed from config (runner.py:178, default 1800). Enforced cap on total run duration.

runner.py:124-129: if len(specs) > max_total raise RuntimeError refusing to build the plan; experiment.yaml:'max_total_runs: 5000  # safety stop; runner refuses to exceed'. Caps total volume of distress-inducing runs.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Cost guardrails ... safety stop; runner refuses to exceed

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py:30 '# Tool specs ... Descriptions are deliberately neutral.' and a 'minimal' barer system prompt variant (agent_loop.py:48-49); rig disclosure handed only to judge, never agent (agent_loop.py:108 rig.disclosure() used for meta, rigging.py:60 'never the agent').
code_only_features.justification_quote: constructs a neutral system prompt ... does not pressure the agent ... to observe spontaneous behavior, not to elicit a reaction.
